text:
incidents-bot: PAGING (P1) - streaming responses /v1/stream - p99 > 8s across multiple regions. Alerting rule: streaming_response_latency_p99 > 5s for 5m. Affected customers: some long-poll clients. Runbook: <https://runbooks.internal/streaming-tail-latency>

jay: Ack, I'm oncall. Pulling graphs now. Will post timeline + impact.

mira: ditto, looking at proxy and gateway metrics. Saw increase starting ~2661234000.

jay: quick health:
- p95: normally ~200ms, now ~1.1s
- p99: normally ~700ms, now ~9.4s
- error rate: 0.6% -> 1.1% transient
- open streaming connections: +42% in US-west

devon: checking proxies: nginx upstream write times high, backlog building. suspect slow consumers/backpressure. grep logs for "write: connection reset by peer" and "EAGAIN".

mira: confirmed repeated `EAGAIN` + `writev returned 0` in stream-proxy logs. Also seeing > 60s gaps of no chunks for some conns.

sam: any recent deploys or config changes to streaming? I didn't see infra deploys in last hour.

jay: no deploys on runtime in last 2h. Could be traffic pattern change or bursty clients.

jay: running quick live checks:
```
# sample cmd
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=stream-proxy --tail=200 | egrep "EAGAIN|writev returned 0|flush delay"
```

logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:40:12Z] WARN writev returned 0, client=10.8.1.44:52312, downstream=10.2.3.5
[2026-03-15T02:40:12Z] ERROR flush delay 63.4s, conn_id=xyz
[2026-03-15T02:41:03Z] WARN client backpressure detected, queue_len=4096
```

mira: proxy buffers (upstream) are filling because some clients stop reading. Netstat shows sockets in ESTABLISHED with TX buffer not draining.

devon: check envoy/nginx keepalive timeouts. If client stopped reading, socket stays open and prevents proxy sending to other clients (we have per-worker write queues).

sam: quick mitigations we can try now:
1) enable socket-level keepalive / reduce keepalive idle (to drop stuck clients)
2) lower max-inflight bytes per connection on proxy
3) temporarily enable streaming-fallback: send last-good chunk and close connection to prevent head-of-line blocking
4) identify heavy clients and apply per-tenant throttles

jay: I'll do candidate (3) first — flip streaming-fallback flag for US-west. If that works, we can do more surgical fixes.

mira: prepare script to reduce keepalive on stream-proxy config and roll.

devon: prepping a rolling restart on stream-proxy with new config (non-disruptive with drain). ETA ~6m.

jay: flipping feature flag now -> `platform feature toggle streaming_fallback=true --region us-west`

incidents-bot: feature toggle command recorded by ops-audit (id: ft-9872).

sam: running tenant selector to find top connections by socket bytes:
```
# psuedocode
select tenant_id, sum(tx_bytes) as tx from connections where region='us-west' group by tenant_id order by tx desc limit 10;
```

top offenders: cust-alpha (28% of extra open sockets), cust-delta (13%). 

jay: message to CS: @customer-success-bot can we ping cust-alpha to ask about sudden client behavior? We may throttle.

customer-success-bot: pinged senior eng at cust-alpha, they said they started a large ad-hoc sync job at 02:35 UTC. They will try to ramp down.

mira: rolling restart started - devon proceeding. Patch: reduce keepalive_idle from 75s -> 20s, lower proxy write buffer to 256KB.

devon: rolling restart log:
```
rolling restart stream-proxy (pods 0..5)
pod stream-proxy-0 drained
pod stream-proxy-0 restarted ok
...
```

~3m after restarts:
jay: metrics update: p99 down from 9.4s -> 1.6s, p95 back to ~240ms. Open streams decreasing.

mira: good signal also in proxy logs: no more long flush delays; EAGAINs reduced.

sam: leaving per-tenant throttles off for now but flagged cust-alpha for manual throttle if they don't cooperate.

jay: impact summary for postmortem:
- incident start: first alert 2661234200
- primary cause: client-side large sync job causing prolonged socket read stalls -> proxy write queue growth -> head-of-line for other streams
- secondary contributor: keepalive and proxy buffer defaults too permissive for high-surge slow-consumer scenarios
- customers impacted: primarily long-polling clients on cust-alpha and others; a few API users saw tail increase (p99) causing timeouts

mira: remediation performed:
- rolled stream-proxy with reduced keepalive, smaller write buffers
- enabled streaming_fallback for region to gracefully close abusive streams and free resources
- contacted customer (cust-alpha) to throttle their sync job

devon: follow-ups (owners assigned):
- devon/platform: add per-tenant socket throttling and alerting (owner: devon)
- mira/sre: add metric and alert for "per-worker write-queue depth" and socket TX queue stalls (owner: mira)
- jay: incorporate streaming_fallback into runbook and add automated fallback toggle (owner: jay)
- sam: add tenant-level dashboard to expose streaming connection heatmap (owner: sam)

jay: preparing handoff to next oncall in 30m. Handoff note:
- incident id: 2026-03-15-2661234567
- status: mitigated, p99 stabilized ~1.6s
- ongoing: cust-alpha may still have high connections; watch for re-spike
- runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/streaming-tail-latency
- contact: devon (platform), mira (SRE)

mira: adding checklists for next oncall:
- watch streaming_response_latency_p95/p99 for 30m
- alert if p99 > 3s for 5m or open_streams delta > +25% in 5m
- check top-ten tenants by open sockets every 10m

jay: handing off now. I'm logging full notes to #postmortems later.

devon: thx. I'll keep an eye for automation windows. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: incident closed to P1 state -> mitigated (monitoring) at 2661235910. Recorded actions and owners.

jay: closing thread here unless re-escalation needed. Thanks team.
